alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list persistent CNS toxicity including insomnia and abnormal dreams as a major adverse event of EFV, warranting substitution. The patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. EFV is a direct cause: symptoms match the guideline-described toxicity and onset follows EFV initiation. No alternative non-drug causes are evident from the clinical notes. The clinician documented the complaints but did not propose a regimen change or further management.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess symptom severity and duration. If persistent CNS toxicity, substitute EFV per guideline toxicity management table and submit aDSM form.

alerts.title: Missing baseline and monitoring labs
alerts.message: No renal function, hepatic panel, or hematological results are recorded for this patient on TDF/3TC/EFV. TDF requires renal monitoring due to nephrotoxicity risk, and EFV requires hepatic monitoring. The clinician's plan does not include any laboratory orders. Viral load was last checked 165 days ago at 60 copies/mL.

evidence.recommended_action: Order creatinine/eGFR, ALT/AST, and HBV screening if not previously done. Schedule viral load per protocol.

alerts.title: Adverse drug reaction reporting not addressed
alerts.message: Guidelines require neuropsychiatric symptoms including bad dreams, insomnia, and anxiety to be screened at each visit and documented on the aDSM form, which should be submitted to the National Drug Authority. The clinician noted insomnia and vivid dreams but the plan does not include aDSM form completion or pharmacovigilance reporting.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete and submit aDSM form to NDA for the patient's EFV-related neuropsychiatric symptoms.
